name: Act of June 22, 1874 ratifying the Sisseton and Wahpeton agreement of September 20, 1872 (18 Stat. 167)
promises: Not a treaty. The Act ratified the agreement of September 20, 1872 for the cession of lands by the Sisseton and Wahpeton (Royce, see area 538).
today: The 1872 agreement itself is recorded as kappler-1065, where no breach was found and the installments were recorded as paid. The Sisseton and Wahpeton later claimed before the Indian Claims Commission (Docket 363) that the 1872 price was unconscionable; in 1975 the Commission upheld their title and ordered a trial on value. The result was not traced.

openQuestions: Not re-counted: the cession of area 538 is the subject of kappler-1065 and of the February 14, 1873 Act (17 Stat. 456) that first confirmed the agreement with amendments.
treaties.json lists no statute for this record; Royce gives 18 Stat. 167. Not edited.

Audit 2026-11-08: the Indian Claims Commission cites this Act as c. 389, 18 Stat. 146, 167 (Docket 363, 36 Ind. Cl. Comm. 472, 1975); citation widened to match. LEAD NOT COUNTED HERE: in Docket 363 (2nd claim, amended) the Sisseton and Wahpeton claimed that the consideration for the lands ceded by the 1872 agreement was unconscionable; on September 25, 1975 the Commission held they had recognized title to the 1867 area and aboriginal title to a southern triangle (northern Royce 410), and sent the case to trial on the value as of May 19, 1873. The outcome (after transfer to the Court of Claims) was not traced. This belongs on kappler-1065, whose audit said no claim over the 1872 agreement was found.
